newsitem.title: USA: Consumers again shuts 780 MW Mich. nuke.
newsitem.headline: Consumers again shuts 780 MW Mich. nuke.

text.p: Consumers Energy said Tuesday it shut the 780 megawatt (MW) Palisades nuclear power plant Monday to repair a leak in a main steam isolation valve and to replace a primary coolant pump seal.
A company spokesman said engineers have not determined how long the plant is likely to be shut for the repair.
"How long that will last it's anyone's guess," he said.
The generating station in South Haven, Mich., facility returned on line briefly yesterday after it was shut Sunday for electrical repairs.
The Palisades plant produces 18 percent of Consumer Energy's total energy output.
The utility said it would have no problem meeting customer demand. "The other units in the system should be able to handle it," he said.
Consumers Energy is a subsidiary of CMS Energy.
